h1: The 5 Best 90-to-100-Inch TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best 90 to 100 Inch TVs 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the best 90 to 100 inch TVs, compared on screen size, refresh rate and panel type, plus one 85 inch step-down option.
summary: The Hisense 100E6QF is the best 90 to 100 inch TV: a 100 inch QLED 4K Fire TV with a stated 144Hz refresh rate, the biggest screen in this ranking. The Samsung DU9000 gives 98 inches at 120Hz with HDR, the TCL Q65 brings QLED and Google TV, and the Samsung U8000H is the 85 inch fallback.
intro: At 98 inches, a TV is a logistics problem before it is a picture problem. The panel is roughly 85 inches wide, and it has to clear your door, climb your stairs and land on a wall or stand built for it. Plan the delivery path first, then argue about contrast and refresh rate. Plenty of buyers discover at the front door that the box does not fit.

We reviewed the 90 to 100 inch TVs available here, plus one 85 inch model as a flagged fallback, ranking them on screen size, refresh rate, panel type and smart platform. Our source data is thin on picture-quality specs, so we kept claims to what the listings state and flagged where a figure is missing. Prices appear as buckets, and every model here sits in the top one.

products.name: Hisense 100" Class E6 Series QLED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV (100E6QF
products.verdict: The biggest screen here, with a 144Hz refresh rate on QLED.
products.description:
The Hisense E6 is a 100 inch QLED 4K Smart Fire TV, and it lists a 144Hz refresh rate. That makes it the largest screen in this ranking and the only one stating 144Hz. A higher refresh rate keeps fast motion sharp in sports and games, and at 100 inches any blur is magnified. It sells in the $500+ bracket.

It ranks first because it pairs the top of the size range with the highest stated refresh rate. Next to the Samsung DU9000, it gives you two more inches and 24 more hertz, though both claims are what the listing states. The TCL Q65 matches its QLED type but lists no refresh rate.

Buy it if you want the biggest screen and care about gaming-friendly refresh. The caveat is size: 100 inches is a delivery and wall challenge. Skip it if your room or doorway cannot take a 100 inch set.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the largest screen and a high refresh rate.
products.skipIf: Your room or doorway cannot take a 100 inch set.

products.name: Samsung 98-Inch Class 4K Crystal UHD DU9000 Series HDR Smart TV
products.verdict: A 98 inch Crystal UHD with 120Hz and HDR.
products.description:
The Samsung DU9000 is a 98 inch Crystal UHD 4K Smart TV with HDR and a stated 120Hz refresh rate. It sells in the $500+ bracket. HDR support widens the gap between bright and dark scenes, which makes a big screen look less flat in a dim room. Crystal UHD is Samsung's LED-based panel, a step apart from quantum-dot QLED.

It ranks second because it offers a slightly smaller footprint than the 100 inch Hisense, which helps in a limited space, while still giving a high refresh rate. It is a Crystal UHD model, whereas the Hisense and TCL list QLED. Against the Samsung Q7F, it states more: a refresh rate and HDR.

Choose it for a big screen with 120Hz in a slightly tighter room. The caveat is that the listing does not state QLED. Skip it if you specifically want QLED.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a big screen with a smaller footprint.

products.name: TCL 98-Inch Q65 QLED 4K UHD Smart TV with Google TV (98Q651G
products.verdict: A 98 inch QLED running Google TV.
products.description:
The TCL Q65 is a 98 inch QLED 4K UHD Smart TV with Google TV built in, and it sells in the $500+ bracket. The listing does not state a refresh rate. A quantum-dot layer is the point of QLED: it widens the range of colors a backlit LCD panel can show, which suits movies and streaming at this size.

It ranks third because the Hisense and the Samsung DU9000 both list high refresh rates, while the TCL does not. It does offer QLED at 98 inches with the Google TV interface, which some buyers prefer to Fire TV or Samsung's own system. Against the Samsung Q7F, it states Google TV and 4K UHD.

Buy it if you prefer Google TV and mostly watch films. The caveat is the missing refresh rate, so gamers should look elsewhere. Skip it if refresh rate is a priority.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want QLED and Google TV.
products.skipIf: High refresh rate is a priority.

products.name: Samsung 98-Inch Class QLED Q7F Series Samsung Vision AI Smart TV
products.verdict: A 98 inch Samsung QLED with Vision AI features.
products.description:
The Samsung Q7F is a 98 inch QLED Smart TV with Samsung Vision AI. Our data does not list its refresh rate or a price bracket. Vision AI is Samsung's label for its smart-feature suite, and the listing offers no more detail on what it does for picture quality. Treat it as a QLED Samsung at the DU9000's size.

It ranks fourth because it states less than the Hisense and DU9000, though it is the Samsung option here with QLED. Against the TCL Q65, it is the same size and panel type but with a different platform and a thinner spec list. The gaps are what lower its score, not any known weakness.

Choose it if you want Samsung and QLED together. The caveat is that you should confirm the refresh rate and current price before buying. Skip it if you need a confirmed refresh rate.
products.idealFor: Samsung buyers who want QLED at 98 inches.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed refresh rate.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class U8000H Series Crystal UHD
products.verdict: An 85 inch fallback if a 98 inch set will not fit.
products.description:
The Samsung U8000H is an 85 inch Crystal UHD 4K TV in the $500+ bracket. It is below the 90 inch floor of this guide, so we include it only as a fallback. Thirteen fewer inches of diagonal makes a real difference at the door: a smaller, lighter panel is easier for two people to carry and mount.

It ranks last because it does not meet the size range, and the listing states only the 85 inch size and 4K. It is the most practical option when delivery or room size rules out 98 inches. Against the DU9000, it gives up 13 inches of diagonal and the stated 120Hz.

Choose it if a 98 or 100 inch set will not fit. The caveat is that it is not a true 90 to 100 inch TV. Skip it if you need a screen of 90 inches or more.

products.skipIf: You need a screen of 90 inches or more.

whatMatters.detail: A 98 inch TV is roughly 85 inches wide, which is wider than many walls and doorways allow. Measure doors, hallways and stairs before ordering, and measure the wall or stand, not just the room. Compare the listed dimensions with your path. A box adds several inches on every side, and turns on stairs need extra room.

Refresh rate is how many times per second the screen updates. 120Hz and 144Hz suit gaming and fast sports, because motion stays crisper. Look for the hertz figure in the title or bullets: the Hisense states 144Hz and the Samsung DU9000 120Hz. The TCL Q65 and Samsung Q7F state none, so treat them as unknown and confirm before you buy.

QLED and Crystal UHD are both LED-backlit LCD technologies. QLED adds a quantum-dot layer that widens color, while Crystal UHD does not. The listing names the type, so confirm it. Neither is an OLED, and at this size both rely on the backlight for brightness, not on perfect black, so room lighting matters more than the label.

Fire TV, Google TV and Samsung's own system differ in apps and layout. Pick the one you already know, because relearning menus on a TV this big is tedious. The platform is named in the product title: Fire TV on the Hisense, Google TV on the TCL, Samsung's system on the Samsung sets. Switching ecosystems later means new remotes and accounts.

A TV this size needs a strong wall mount or a wide stand, and the stand must be as wide as the feet. Check the weight and VESA details on the listing. Plan for two people to lift it, and check the wall studs before you drill. Stand width is easy to overlook, and a narrow stand can make a 98 inch set unstable.

faq.q: Will a 98 inch TV fit through my door?
faq.a: Measure first. A 98 inch TV is roughly 85 inches wide, so check doorways, hallways and stair turns, and remember that the box adds more. Ask the seller what delivery service is included.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make at this size?
faq.a: They plan the picture but not the delivery. Measure the path and wall before ordering, whether you choose the Hisense 100 inch or a 98 inch Samsung or TCL. The panel is usually delivered in a very large box.

faq.q: Is the Hisense worth it over the Samsung DU9000?
faq.a: If you want two more inches and a stated 144Hz, yes. The Samsung is a slightly smaller footprint with 120Hz and HDR, and uses Crystal UHD rather than QLED.

faq.q: How do I set up a TV this large?
faq.a: Use a heavy-duty wall mount or a wide stand and bring a helper, ideally two people. Follow the manual for weight guidance, and fix into studs, not drywall alone, for any of these 98 and 100 inch sets.

faq.q: How do I maintain a large screen?
faq.a: Dust with a microfiber cloth and avoid sprays. Check the manual for cleaning advice, and keep vents clear on the Hisense, TCL and Samsung sets. Unplug the set before wiping, and never press on the panel.
It is a practical fallback, but it is below the 90 inch range of this guide. The Samsung U8000H is 85 inches, 13 inches smaller than the DU9000, so choose it only when delivery rules out larger sets.

finalTake: Buy the Hisense 100E6QF if you want the largest screen and the highest stated refresh rate, and your room and doorway can take it. Choose the Samsung DU9000 for a slightly smaller footprint, the TCL Q65 for Google TV and QLED, and the 85 inch Samsung only when 98 inches will not fit. Measure the path before you pick the panel.
